subject.title: [Feature]: Conversation identity modes for personal, team, and shared audiences

question: Should OpenClaw adopt the proposed closed personal/team/external audience contract, with unresolved and guest audiences denied before personal identity, workspace, and instructions are loaded?
rationale: The merged prerequisites provide trusted scope facts, but selecting the permanent identity boundary and its fail-closed semantics is a product and security policy decision rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Sponsor the closed audience contract
options.body: Define trusted audience inputs and require all ingress paths to deny unresolved or external conversations before personal context resolution.

options.title: Narrow to ingress hardening
options.body: Land only the raw-ingress guard and defer organization/team identity semantics until a separate product design is approved.

options.title: Keep existing routing semantics
options.body: Retain current behavior and document that personal-context routing remains an operator-managed deployment responsibility.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the closed audience contract
recommendation.body: Define trusted audience inputs and require all ingress paths to deny unresolved or external conversations before personal context resolution.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue author also carried the merged profile and trusted-scope prerequisites and is linked to the active implementation path.
